narr: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred across North Central Alabama from the afternoon of June 7th through the evening of June 8th. The activity was the result several upper-level disturbances moving over a slow moving surface front. Some storms were strong to severe at times with damaging wind gusts, as well as large hail. Many of these thunderstorms went on to evolve into clusters that were slow moving, or nearly stationary at times. The slow moving or training nature of these thunderstorms, along with torrential rainfall rates, led to flash flooding. The most significant flash flooding occurred on the morning of June 8th. Slow moving thunderstorms produced near six inches of rain in areas such as Birmingham and Sylacauga. Some additional flash flooding occurred on the evening of June 8th across portions of Birmingham. In total, the Birmingham International Airport measured 6.97 of rainfall on June 8th, breaking the daily rainfall record and placing this as the 6th highest daily rainfall ever recorded at Birmingham.
ev: Several road closures due to high water along Valleydale Road and Highway 119 in northern Shelby County. Inverness Landing Apartments on Valleydale Road reported multiple units with water up to waist deep.
County Road 22 at Summerchase Parkway impassable due to high water.
Widespread flooding in the city of Sylacauga with water entering buildings and several roads closed.
Several roads flooded and impassable in the city of Jacksonville.
Flooding reported along Highway 78 in Adamsville with several vehicles stalled out in high water.

Back-building thunderstorms produced significant rainfall amounts across eastern Etowah County. The heaviest rainfall totals were along Highway 431 between Gadsden and Glencoe. Many roads were flooded and impassable in both cities with water recues reported at an apartment complex in Glencoe due to high water.

Widespread heavy rainfall and flooding across southern Jefferson County, mainly along and south of I-20 and along and east of I-65. Numerous roads flooded and impassable in the cities of Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Hoover, Downtown Birmingham and Mountain Brook. Village Creek At Avenue W in Birmingham rose above flood stage (10 Feet) at crested at 13 feet, causing major flooding in this area.

Several roads flooded and impassable across eastern Jefferson County along Highway 75 near Center Point. Several cars submerged near Sweeney Hollow Road and a water rescue from a home in the same area. Shadow Lake Road flooded and impassable.
Several roads flooded and impassable around the city of Vincent. Several vehicles stalled out with one almost completely submerged.
